- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.2) and price is trending up, model often fails to reverse; adjust downward by 1–2% if sentiment drops below 0.3.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is weak (≤0.2) and price is volatile; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast if sentiment <0.2 and 3-day moving avg is rising.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits recent momentum; apply mean reversion: if 10-day moving avg is >10% above 30-day avg, reduce forecast by 1–2%.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.2–0.5) and price is flat, model tends to drift upward; cap forecast at 1% above prior 7-day high if sentiment remains flat.
